old: Removes the 2030 end date on the higher income tax rates for income over about $371,000 for single filers, adjusted yearly for inflation. Rates themselves do not change.
new: Makes permanent the higher income tax rates on income over about $371,000 for single filers, adjusted yearly for inflation. The rates now apply through 2030 and are set to expire in 2031. Rates themselves do not change.
reason: The page said 'Removes the 2030 end date' here and 'expiring in 2031' in YES and NO. Both dates are official. LAO, prop3-title-summ-analysis.pdf page 26: 'In 2016, voters approved Proposition 55 to extend these higher rates until 2030.' Page 27 and the Attorney General summary: 'expire in 2031' and 'currently set to expire in 2031.' The legal text applies the rates to tax years 'before January 1, 2031' (evc-prop3-does-3). One sentence now gives both. When applied, update the claim text of evc-prop3-does-1 to -4 to the new wording.

old: A $50 million clinic at 80% would owe $5 million that year. LAO estimates state enforcement costs of low tens of millions of dollars a year, covered by fees on clinics.
new: A $50 million clinic at 80% would owe $5 million that year (this tool's example, using the 90% rule). LAO estimates state enforcement costs of low tens of millions of dollars a year, covered by fees on clinics.
reason: The example is this tool's arithmetic and is now labeled like the Prop 37 example. LAO: 'The penalty would equal the amount of spending needed to reach the 90 percent minimum.' (90% minus 80%) times $50 million is $5 million. Ledger row evc-prop44-money-1.
